title: Stitchboard: Roadmap synthesis + pre-sync notes (Product / Eng / Applied ML)
content:
Purpose: quick prep and synthesis for the cross-functional roadmap alignment sync. Goal is to surface the real tradeoffs we need Product + Eng + Applied ML to decide on (latency SLOs vs unit cost, model variant support vs rollout complexity, observability requirements that block canary strategies).

Meeting background/context:
- Product has asked for a tightened latency target for chat endpoints (p95 target from 450ms -> 300ms) for featured customers; this would materially change capacity and possibly require model quantization/optimized kernels.
- Eng (serving-runtime) has a queued kernel optimization (attn-fastpath) on the roadmap but will not be ready for general rollout until mid-July.
- Applied ML recommends two model variants: baseline open-llama-70b (fp16) and a quantized 4-bit variant with known degradation on long-context coherence. They suggest targeted reranker fallback for QA flows.
- Constraints: Dedicated capacity commitments for two enterprise customers (contract terms restrict abrupt model swaps), and limited SRE bandwidth for major rollout in June.

High-level sync objective for this meeting:
1) Agree on a minimal set of roadmap decisions to unblock engineering work in the next two sprints.
2) Surface and assign follow-ups for risk mitigation (canary plan, eval prompts, rollback hooks).
3) Align on milestone acceptance criteria (SLOs, cost uplift tolerances, eval thresholds).

Proposed meeting agenda (30–40m):
- 0–5m quick framing (why we need agreement now) — Jeremy
- 5–12m Product presents customer asks and commercial trigger points — Maya
- 12–22m Eng presents feasibility and schedule (kernel timelines, infra impacts) — Diego
- 22–30m Applied ML presents quality tradeoffs and suggested mitigations (reranker, prompt-level thresholds) — Lucia
- 30–35m Decision points and owners (capture explicit yes/no + follow-ups) — all
- 35–40m Quick risks + rollback checklist — SRE rep (if present)

Key decision points we need to resolve in the sync (with my preliminary recommendation):
1) Latency target scope: narrow to interactive features only (chat and assistant) vs platform-wide. Recommendation: narrow scope to interactive features for Q3 pilot to limit infra churn.
2) Model variant plan: support both baseline fp16 and quantized 4-bit across Hosted API, but only enable 4-bit for Dedicated after canary. Recommendation: staged enablement; quantized only for non-contracted tenants initially.
3) Canary strategy: time-boxed canary with per-route rollback and automated quality regression alerts using eval prompt set. Recommendation: 2-week canary on 5% traffic with daily evals and immediate rollback threshold set at >3% deviance on critical prompts.
4) Observability surface: need token-level cost tagging + per-request model variant metadata in traces to diagnose regressions quickly. Recommendation: short spike to add model variant tag to trace headers (owner: Eng / telemetry).

Open assumptions to validate during meeting (and who to validate):
- SLO impact estimate accuracy (Eng to produce revised cost and capacity numbers by 2026-05-14).
- Quality delta of quantized 4-bit on long prompts (Applied ML to produce 50-sample focused evaluation on our internal eval harness by 2026-05-15).
- Contract risk for Dedicated tenants if default variant toggles change (Customer Success + Legal to confirm guardrails; owner: Maya; due 2026-05-17).

Preliminary tradeoff matrix (for discussion):
- Option A (aggressive): Move platform p95 to 300ms and enable 4-bit across hosted. Pros: customer satisfaction, competitive positioning. Cons: higher rollout risk, potential quality regressions, infra cost to retool.
- Option B (staged): Target only interactive features; staged variant rollout; canary + reranker in front. Pros: lower risk, measurable rollback. Cons: slower time to value, complexity in routing.
- Option C (conservative): Delay changes until attn-fastpath kernel lands. Pros: lower engineering effort; Cons: misses customer window.

Concrete follow-ups to assign now (short list):
- Eng: produce updated capacity and cost delta table for 300ms p95 scenario (fields: GPUs required, per-token cost uplift, infra changes). Due 2026-05-14. Owner: Diego Ramos.
- Applied ML: run 50 targeted long-context evals comparing fp16 vs 4-bit; produce short doc with recommended fallback prompts and thresholds. Due 2026-05-15. Owner: Lucia Chen.
- Product/Legal/Customer Success: confirm contractual constraints for Dedicated model variant changes; list tenants with restrictions. Due 2026-05-17. Owner: Maya Singh.
- SRE/Observability: quick spike to add model-variant trace tag + token-cost breakdown per request, and ship a tracing dashboard prototype. Due 2026-05-20. Owner: Priya Patel (SRE).
- Jeremy (me): consolidate meeting notes + decision record, update roadmap doc and push to Confluence. Due 2026-05-13.

Risks & mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Quality regression after quantized rollout. Mitigation: per-route reranker fallback (detect critical failure patterns via eval prompts; roll traffic back to fp16).
- Risk: Contract breach for Dedicated customers. Mitigation: explicit allowlist for variant changes; communicate maintenance window with CS.
- Risk: SRE capacity. Mitigation: limit initial scope to interactive endpoints; use canary % to contain blast radius.

Quick notes for the sync facilitator (Jeremy):
- Start with one clear ask: a binary decision on scoping (interactive-only vs platform-wide). Keep the conversation focused — avoid deep kernel design debates in this forum; route those to a follow-up techncial deep-dive with Eng/Runtime.
- If the group stalls on quantization acceptance, push to accept staged plan (Option B) with committed follow-ups rather than forcing a full yes today.

Artifacts to bring to the meeting (links / attachments):
- 1-page customer impact memo (short bullets).
- Preliminary cost delta table (stubbed numbers) — Eng should bring roughs.
- Eval harness sample prompts (Applied ML).
- Current SLAs and Dedicated contract excerpts (CS/Legal).

Suggested phrasing for decision capture (so Confluence record is tidy):
- Decision: Scope latency target to interactive features (chat/assistant) for Q3 pilot. Owner: Product. Date: 2026-05-12.
- Decision: Approve staged quantized variant rollout for Hosted API; do not enable for contracted Dedicated tenants without explicit signoff. Owner: Eng + Applied ML. Date: 2026-05-12.
- Action: Create canary plan with eval thresholds and rollback rules. Owner: Eng + Applied ML + SRE. Due: 2026-05-20.

My personal notes / heuristics to keep the meeting productive:
- Push for measurable acceptance criteria (exact eval metrics, exact SLO numbers, cost tolerances).
- Avoid making the rollout all-or-nothing — always prefer gated rollout + telemetry hooks.
- When faced with quality variance, prefer automated fallback (reranker/route) over manual on-call intervention.

Bottom line (one-line summary to start the meeting):
We need a scoped, staged plan that gets customers lower latency without exposing contracted tenants to unacceptable quality or contractual risk — agree on interactive-only scope and staged quantization canary today, with concrete deliverables in the next 10 business days.

-- end of scratchboard --

(If helpful I can also pre-populate a Confluence decision record and a Linear epic with the follow-ups prior to the meeting.)
